adults.title: Not Earned, Never Lost
adults.big_idea: Heavenly Father's love for each of His children was never earned and cannot be lost, and understanding it draws us to Jesus Christ and His covenants.
adults.objective: Learners will be able to explain how understanding Heavenly Father's love changes the way they see the Savior, other people, and their own chance to change, and will choose one way to act on it this week.
prepare: Read Elder Fale's talk, especially the baby-picture story and his three reasons for understanding our Father's love.
Bring one baby picture: your own, a family member's, or any picture of a newborn.
Write on the board two headings, Truth and Twist, and below them the numbers 1, 2, 3.
Have paper and pens for silent writing.

segments.name: A baby picture
steps: After the prayer, hold up the baby picture. Ask the first question below and take two or three short answers.

Tell Elder Fale's story in your own words: during a Church meeting he felt prompted to do what the teacher was doing, so he texted his wife and asked her to find a baby picture of each of their children. At home they showed the children their pictures. He told them no words could fully express the love he and his wife felt when each was born, then asked what they had done by that day to earn it. They lowered their eyes and answered, Nothing.
Read what he told them next (the first key quote). Let it sit for a moment before moving on.
questions: What had this baby done, by the day this picture was taken, to earn anyone's love?

segments.name: A small fraction
steps: Explain that Elder Fale told his children that what parents feel is only a small fraction of what Heavenly Father feels for them. Invite someone to read the second and third key quotes aloud.

Say gently that Elder Fale knew families differ. He taught that for some the picture may be a sibling, a grandparent, or only a desire for a family, and that even when a loving family is not part of our experience here, knowing Heavenly Father loves us can give power, peace, and comfort.
Invite learners to turn to one person nearby and share an answer to one of the questions below. Give three minutes, then ask one or two to share with the class.
questions: When has knowing you are a child of God given you courage to do your best or to trust Him?
Elder Fale hoped this truth would give his children the strength and humility to come home when they need to. Why does coming home take both?

segments.name: The truth and the twist
steps: Point to the two headings. Explain that Elder Fale followed his witness with a warning: the adversary twists this truth, hoping we will believe that because God loves us we can be saved regardless of pride, rebellion, sin, or rejecting His Son and His Son's servants.
Ask the class to help you fill in the two columns in a few words each. Under Truth: loved before we did anything; love that cannot be lost. Under Twist: so nothing is asked of me.
Read the fourth key quote together. Then read Elder Gilbert's sentence from this conference (the second aligned quote).
Read John 3:16 together and ask what the Father's love gave and what it invites us to do.
Check understanding: ask one learner to say, in a single sentence, the difference between the truth and the twist.
questions: Why does knowing we are loved make covenants matter more to us, not less?

segments.name: Three reasons
steps: Divide into three groups (or three pairs). Assign each group one of Elder Fale's three reasons, found in the three paragraphs of the talk that begin First, Second, and Third.
Group 1 reads the first reason with Matthew 7:9–11: understanding the Father's love helps us understand Jesus Christ and makes us eager to join His work.

Group 2 reads the second reason: we become immune to the divisive labels of the world, quick to repent, slow to judge, and watchful that no one is alone. Give this group President Chibota's sentence (the first aligned quote).
Group 3 reads the third reason with Luke 15:20: we are protected from the lie that it is too late for someone to change or turn to Christ.
Give five minutes for groups to discuss the two questions below. Then give each group one minute to report while you write a few of their words beside 1, 2, and 3 on the board.
questions: What does understanding Heavenly Father's love change, according to this paragraph?
Where would that change show up in an ordinary week: at home, at work, or at church?

segments.name: Which one do I need?
steps: Hand out paper. Invite learners to write silently for three minutes: Which of the three reasons do I most need right now? Is there a label I need to put down, a person I have quietly decided is too late, or a step back toward the Savior I have put off?
Ask them to finish by writing one specific thing they will do before next Sunday. Suggest the ideas in the act list if anyone is unsure. No one needs to share what they wrote.

segments.name: Witness and follow-up
steps: Tell how Elder Fale first learned this as a young boy, riding from Nuku‘alofa to his home village of Mu‘a and reading John 3:16 in a New Testament. He said he knew it was true then and knows it is true now.

Remind the class of what he taught this understanding brings: it is essential for our daily and eternal happiness, it prevents deception, and it gives purpose to mortal life. Bear your own brief testimony that each person in the room is a child of God.
Tell the class that next week you will begin by asking what happened when they acted on what they wrote.

key_quotes.text: You did not earn it; you cannot lose it. It is yours forever.
He loved you before you were born, He loves you today, and He will love you tomorrow.
no matter what has happened, you can always come home, just as you can always turn to your Father in Heaven.
Receiving Christ through priesthood ordinances and covenants, and then being faithful to those covenants, is the only way for us to fully understand His love and the only way to exaltation.

scriptures.use: Read together in the truth-and-twist segment; ask what the Father's love gave and what it invites us to do. Return to it at the close with Elder Fale's boyhood witness.
Group 1 reads it with the first reason and asks what the Savior wanted us to know about the Father He came to serve.
Group 3 reads it with the third reason; look for what the father does while the son is still a long way off.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Chibota
aligned_quotes.text: Our identity is not something we achieve; it is something we inherit as beloved sons and daughters of God.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Gilbert
aligned_quotes.text: For disciples of Jesus Christ, truth and love always walk together.

takeaways: I did nothing to earn Heavenly Father's love, and nothing can remove it.
His love does not excuse sin; it leads me to Jesus Christ and to keeping my covenants.
It is not too late for me or for anyone I love to turn to Christ today.
act: Each morning this week, begin your prayer by thanking Heavenly Father that you are His child, and notice what changes in the rest of the prayer.
Name one label you have placed on yourself or on someone else, and each time it comes to mind replace it with the words child of God.
Think of one person you have quietly decided will never change. Pray for that person by name every day and reach out once in a simple way.
Look around at church or at work for someone sitting, standing, or walking alone, and join them.
music: I Am a Child of God
adapt: At home: use baby pictures of those present, if that suits your household, and let each person choose one of the three reasons to read and explain. Skip the board.
Large class: do the three reasons by rows instead of groups, and take one report from each section of the room.
Short on time: keep the baby picture, the truth and the twist, and the silent writing. Summarize the three reasons yourself in one minute.

youth.title: The Label That Outranks the Rest
youth.big_idea: I am a child of God who was loved before I did anything, and that truth is stronger than any label the world puts on me or on anyone else.
youth.objective: Youth will be able to explain why Heavenly Father's love is not earned and why their choices still matter, and will choose one way this week to live as a child of God among children of God.
prepare: Read Elder Fale's talk. Know the baby-picture story well enough to tell it without notes.
Bring sticky notes or small slips of paper with tape, pens, and one full sheet of paper with CHILD OF GOD written large.
Bring a baby picture of yourself if you have one. It makes a good start.
Ask youth to have their scriptures or the Gospel Library app ready.
Write on the board: John 3:16, Matthew 6:9, Matthew 7:9–11.

segments.name: Sixty seconds of labels
steps: As soon as the prayer ends, hand out sticky notes and pens. Give exactly sixty seconds: write as many labels as you can that the world puts on people your age, one per note. Keep them general, not about any real person (for example: popular, awkward, smart, not good enough).
Have everyone stick their notes on the board. Read several aloud without comment.
Ask the question below and take two quick answers. Say that you will come back to the board.
questions: Which kind of label is harder to shake off: one that someone else gives you or one you give yourself?

segments.name: What had you done?
steps: Show your baby picture if you brought one. Tell Elder Fale's story: in a Church meeting he felt prompted to do what the teacher was doing, so he texted his wife to find a baby picture of each of their children. At home he showed the children their pictures, told them no words could fully express the love their parents felt the day they were born, and asked what they had done by that day to earn it. They looked down and answered, Nothing.
Ask a youth to read the first key quote. Then tell them what he said next: what parents feel is only a small fraction of what Heavenly Father feels for them. Read the second key quote.
Ask the questions below. Listen more than you talk. Acknowledge, as Elder Fale did, that not everyone has a loving family, and that Heavenly Father's love is real for every person in the room.
questions: Most things in your life are earned: grades, a spot on the team, followers. Why is it hard to believe in love you cannot earn?
What would change in a person who really believed this love cannot be lost?

segments.name: Six-word summaries
steps: Put youth in pairs or threes and assign each team one reference from the board. With more than three teams, give the same verse to two teams.
Each team reads its verses in their scriptures or the app and writes a summary of exactly six words of what the passage teaches about Heavenly Father. Give three minutes.
Each team reads its six words aloud. The class votes for the best summary by pointing, and no one may vote for their own team.
Tell them Elder Fale read John 3:16 as a young boy, riding from Nuku‘alofa to his home village of Mu‘a, and the Holy Spirit witnessed to him that it was true. Read the third key quote.
questions: Elder Fale pointed out that Jesus taught us to pray to our Father, not only His Father. What does that one word say about who you are?

segments.name: Two honest questions
steps: Say that Elder Fale's talk speaks to two questions people really ask. Ask the first question below and let youth respond before you teach.

Explain his warning: the adversary twists the truth of God's love into a lie that we can be saved regardless of our pride, rebellion, or sins, or of rejecting the Savior and His servants. Elder Fale taught that receiving Christ through ordinances and covenants, and being faithful to them, is the only way to fully understand God's love and the only way to exaltation. Being loved is where we start. It is not a reason to stay where we are.
Ask the second question. Then read the fourth key quote. Elder Fale called the idea that it is too late a lie, and he pointed to the prodigal son and the one lost sheep.
Check understanding: ask a volunteer to answer both questions in one sentence each, as if a friend had asked.
questions: If God loves me no matter what, do my choices really matter?
Can a person mess up so badly, or wait so long, that it is too late to turn to Christ?

segments.name: No one alone
steps: Go back to the board. Explain that Elder Fale taught that when we understand God's love we become immune to the world's labels, see everyone as beloved and divine, and make sure no one is sitting, standing, or walking alone.
Invite a youth to place the CHILD OF GOD sheet over the sticky notes so that it covers them. Read Sister Muñoz Spannaus's words, spoken to the young women at this conference (the aligned quote).

In groups of three, give two minutes to plan a twenty-second scene: one person is sitting alone at lunch, standing alone at a youth activity, or walking alone in the hall. Show what someone who sees a child of God would actually say and do. Keep it real, not cheesy.
Watch two or three scenes. After each, ask the class what made it believable.

segments.name: Choose and write
steps: Invite each youth to type or write Elder Fale's opening sentence where they will see it every day, such as a phone note, a lock screen, or a card in their scriptures: “I am a child of God and He loves me.”
Show the act list and ask each to choose one challenge for the week. Have them tell their choice to the person beside them.

Share what Elder Fale hoped this truth would give his own children: courage to do their best, to trust Heavenly Father, and to live up to their potential, and the strength and humility to come home when they need to. Bear a short testimony.
Tell them you will ask next week what happened, and then do it.

key_quotes.text: You did not earn it; you cannot lose it. It is yours forever.
He loved you before you were born, He loves you today, and He will love you tomorrow.
God’s love is real, and Jesus Christ is evidence of that love.
there is still yet time if we turn to Christ today.

scriptures.use: One team reads it and writes a six-word summary. Then tell how Elder Fale gained his witness reading this verse as a boy.
One team reads verse 9 and writes a six-word summary; ask what the word our says about who we are.
One team reads it and writes a six-word summary of what kind of Father gives these gifts.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Sister Muñoz Spannaus
aligned_quotes.text: knowing everything about you does not make Him love you less

takeaways: I did not earn Heavenly Father's love, and I cannot lose it.
Because He loves me, He gave His Son and asks me to follow Him; my choices matter.
Everyone I meet is a child of God, and no one should be left alone.
act: Every morning this week, before you open any app, say out loud: I am a child of God and He loves me.
Find one person who is sitting, standing, or walking alone at school or at church, and join them. Do it at least twice.
When you catch yourself putting a label on someone, or on yourself, replace it in your mind with child of God.
If something in your life needs to be made right, do not wait. Pray tonight, and talk with a parent or your bishop this week.
music: I Am a Child of God
adapt: At home: skip the vote and the scenes. Do the labels on one sheet of paper, tell the story, read John 3:16 together, and let each person choose a challenge.
Small class (two to four youth): work as one team on all three scriptures and talk through one scenario instead of acting it out.
Short on time: keep the labels, the baby-picture story, the two honest questions, and the challenge.

children.title: Heavenly Father Loves Me Always
children.big_idea: I am a child of God, and He loves me.
children.objective: Children will be able to say, I am a child of God and He loves me, and will choose to say it in their prayers this week.
prepare: Read the baby-picture story in Elder Fale's talk so you can tell it in a few simple sentences.
Bring a picture of a baby (from a Church magazine, the Gospel Library, or one you draw) and a picture of Jesus Christ.
Bring a flashlight, a soft ball, plain paper, and crayons.
Before class, draw a large heart on a sheet of paper for each child.
Write on the board or a paper: I am a child of God, and He loves me.

segments.name: Sing and say
steps: Sing the first verse of “I Am a Child of God” together and invite a child to pray.
Teach today's truth with actions: I am a child of God (point to yourself, then point up), and He loves me (hug yourself).
Say it together three times: in a big voice, in a small voice, then in a whisper.

segments.name: The baby picture
steps: Show the picture of the baby. Ask the first question below. Let the children answer and show you with actions: sleep, cry, wiggle.
Ask: Can a baby sweep the floor? Carry a heavy box? Read a book? Let them answer No each time.

Tell the story: Elder Fale is a leader in the Church. One day he showed his children pictures of themselves as tiny babies. He told them how much he and their mother loved them on the day they were born. He asked what they had done to earn that love. They said, Nothing. He told them they were right. They did not earn it, and they cannot lose it.
Tell them the most important part: Elder Fale said Heavenly Father loves us even more than that. Say the truth together with the actions.
questions: What can a tiny baby do?
Did Elder Fale's children have to do something special first to be loved?

segments.name: Before, today, tomorrow
steps: Have the children stand in a line across the room. Name one side of the room Before, the middle Today, and the other side Tomorrow.

Dim the lights if you can. Hold the flashlight and tell them the light is like Heavenly Father's love. Lead the children to the Before side and shine the light on the wall there. Say: Heavenly Father loved you before you were born.
Tiptoe together to the middle and shine the light there. Say: He loves you today. March to the other side and shine it there. Say: He will love you tomorrow.
Do it once more, faster, and let the children say the three sentences with you. Let a child hold the flashlight this time.
Sit down and ask the question below.
questions: Is there any day when Heavenly Father does not love you?

segments.name: Heavenly Father sent Jesus
steps: Show the picture of Jesus Christ. Open your scriptures to John 3:16 and tell the children these are the words Elder Fale read when he was a young boy: “For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son.”
Explain in simple words: Heavenly Father loves us so much that He sent Jesus to help us come back home to Him.
Tell them Jesus taught us how to pray, and He taught us to call Heavenly Father our Father. Have the children fold their arms and practice the first words of a prayer together: Dear Heavenly Father.
Sing “My Heavenly Father Loves Me.”
questions: How do you know Heavenly Father loves you?

segments.name: Draw me in the heart
steps: Give each child a paper with a heart and some crayons. Invite them to draw themselves inside the heart.
Help them write or trace across the top: I am a child of God.
While they draw, walk around and say to each child by name: You are a child of God, and He loves you.
When most are finished, ask the question below. Then invite them to add one more person inside the heart, someone they can be kind to this week.
questions: Who else is a child of God? (Everyone.)

segments.name: No one left out
steps: Sit in a circle on the floor. Tell the children Elder Fale taught that when we know God loves everyone, we make sure no one is left alone.
Roll the ball to one child and say: (Name) is a child of God. That child rolls it to someone who has not had a turn, and everyone says the sentence with the new name.
Keep going until every child, and every teacher, has had the ball. Point out that no one was left out.

segments.name: Remember and do
steps: Stand and say the truth one more time with the actions.
Tell the children in a sentence or two that you know they are children of God and that He loves them.
Invite them to say, I am a child of God, to Heavenly Father when they pray tonight, and to put their drawing where they will see it. Tell them you will ask next week who remembered.

key_quotes.text: I am a child of God and He loves me.
You did not earn it; you cannot lose it. It is yours forever.
He loved you before you were born, He loves you today, and He will love you tomorrow.

scriptures.use: Open to it and read the first part aloud, as quoted in the talk, while showing a picture of Jesus. Explain that Heavenly Father sent Jesus because He loves us.
Show the children verse 9, where Jesus taught us to call Heavenly Father our Father, then practice the first words of a prayer. An older child can read the verse.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Sister Muñoz Spannaus
aligned_quotes.text: knowing everything about you does not make Him love you less

takeaways: I am a child of God.
Everyone is a child of God, so I can be kind.
act: When you pray tonight, tell Heavenly Father: I am Thy child. Thank Him for loving you.
Put your heart drawing by your bed and say the truth each morning.
Find someone who is alone and invite them to play or sit with you.
music: I Am a Child of God

adapt.younger: Ages 3–7: keep each part short and repeat the truth with actions after every activity. Tell the baby story in three sentences. Let helpers hold the flashlight and the pictures. If drawing is hard, let children color the heart and place a hand inside it while you say their name and the truth. Sing the song a second time if they get restless.
adapt.older: Ages 8–11: have a child read John 3:16 and Matthew 6:9 aloud, and let one lead the flashlight walk and another lead the ball game. Ask a harder question: If Heavenly Father loves us no matter what, why does He still ask us to follow Jesus and keep our promises to Him? Help them see that because He loves us, He gave us the Savior and the way back home to Him. You may read Sister Muñoz Spannaus's words in the aligned quote and ask how it feels to know that. Have them write on the back of the drawing one way to make sure no one is alone this week.
